# `request-body-removed`

Request body removed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `warn` |
| **Rule IDs** | `request-body-removed` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M3) |
| **Group** | Request bodies ([RULES.md section 5](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

An operation no longer documents a request body.

## Why this default

Clients still send one. Most servers ignore it, so the data is silently dropped; some reject it.

## Example

From test case [`request-body-removed`](../../test/cases/request-body-removed/): Body removed: clients still send one, so it is a warning.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
      post:
        operationId: createPet
-       requestBody:
-         content:
-           application/json:
-             schema:
-               type: object
        responses:
          '200':
```

Findings:

- `request-body-removed` · warn · POST /pets

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  request-body-removed: warn
```

## How to fix

Keep accepting the body until clients stop sending it, or version the operation.
